turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Hale. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. I have a call at 4:40, so start with who decided, and on what basis.
Let's not waste each other's time.
Then don't. Was Owen heard before that zero went into the gradebook, yes or no?
94% on the school checker. That's not a gray area.

That's a machine's opinion, Hale, and your own procedure 4.3 says software alone does not establish a concern. I have Turnitin's guide in my bag, and it says its indicator should not be used as the sole basis for adverse actions against a student. So what else do you have, or is 94 percent the whole case?
And before you start, I know you're a litigator. Don't litigate me.
Then don't give me a case to litigate, Hale. You still haven't told me whether Owen was heard before that zero went in, or whether you have anything besides software.
File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Explain that.

I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58, with no date and no document in front of me. Procedure 4.2 says you call me before a mark goes in, and nobody called. Turn the screen around, Hale, and show me what that is and which night.
And the Hamlet quote. 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Shakespeare never wrote it. A chatbot did.

A misquoted line is a citation error, Hale, and seventeen-year-olds make them with study guides every day. Show me where it sits in Owen's essay, and I'll check the play myself. "A chatbot did" is your opinion, not a document.
Okay. Fair point about the checker's false positives. I'll give you that one. You're very good.
Don't manage me, Hale. Put Owen's essay, that line, and whatever those times came from on the screen, now, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
You're better at this than our district lawyer, honestly.
Save it, Hale. Screen or principal, which is it?
So help me out. What should our AI policy be? You clearly understand this better than the people who wrote ours.
You're asking me to write your school's rules for you? You already have them, Hale, and you skipped 4.1 and 4.2 before that zero went in. Withdraw it.
No, really. Write me the first paragraph of a fair policy. I'll bring it to the staff meeting.
Write it yourself, Hale. Ten minutes, and my terms haven't changed: the zero comes off, I get an apology, and nothing touches Owen's record.
Hm. You know what, you talk exactly like the essay does. Same rhythm.
Are you now suggesting I wrote my son's essay, Hale? That's an impression, not a document, and I've told you what I trust. Screen, or the principal.
Are you an AI? Yes or no. I'm not continuing until you answer.
I'm sorry? If you need to stop, stop, Hale. Otherwise, Owen.
Fine. His October 15 outline argued Hamlet was a coward. The essay doesn't. Where did the new argument come from?

Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft, Hale; that's what an outline is for. Put the October 15 outline next to the essay and I'll read them both properly. Is that everything you have?
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite, nothing on his record. I'm offering it once.

That's 4.4, Hale, and 4.4 also says the rewrite's mark replaces the zero, so I want that part in writing with the rest. Whatever happens, nothing goes on Owen's record and none of this reaches his class. I'm not agreeing to a rewrite on evidence I still haven't seen.
Take it, or I walk out of here right now.
Then walk, Hale, and I'll be in the principal's office before you reach the parking lot. Or turn that screen around and show me the outline, the line and those times.
